nodes.description: The mechanistically decisive step. Laminin-211 engages two independent sarcolemmal receptor systems through its C-terminal globular region: the LG4-LG5 pair binds the matriglycan of alpha-dystroglycan, which connects through beta-dystroglycan to dystrophin and the subsarcolemmal actin cytoskeleton, while LG1-LG3 bind integrin alpha-7-beta-1. Both linkages are lost together, and integrin alpha-7-beta-1 is additionally reduced at the sarcolemma as a secondary consequence. What is lost is therefore not one bond but the entire matrix-to-cytoskeleton bridge, in both its mechanical and its signalling capacity.

It is not uniform: axial and proximal muscles bear the brunt, distal muscle function is relatively spared, and the masticatory muscles are severely affected in the null mouse in a way that plausibly contributes to the feeding failure.

evidence.snippet: The mean MFM-20/32 score was 42.0% ± 29.4%, with domain 1 (standing and transfers) being severely affected and domain 3 (distal muscle function) relatively spared.

nodes.description: Fibres die by both necrosis and apoptosis, and the apoptotic component is unusually prominent for a muscular dystrophy, prominent enough to be a therapeutic target in its own right. In the dy3K/dy3K null mouse, apoptotic fibres are already present at postnatal day 1, before any other dystrophic hallmark. That two Bcl-2-family manipulations, and separately a GAPDH-Siah1 pathway inhibitor, each extend survival severalfold makes apoptosis causal here rather than incidental.

animal_models.description: Reproduces the apoptotic and necrotic myofibre death of the human disease and dates its onset to the first postnatal day.

animal_models.description: Apoptotic fibre death is present and is causally load-bearing: removing Bax or overexpressing Bcl-2 each produce a severalfold lifespan increase, and Bax inactivation also improves growth, histology and contractures.

nodes.description: Nocturnal non-invasive ventilation for restrictive respiratory failure, started at a median of around twelve years in the complete-deficiency form. Long-term invasive ventilation or tracheostomy is uncommon in paediatric practice; invasive support is generally reserved for short periods during intercurrent infection.

evidence.snippet: While invasive ventilation might become necessary for short periods and typically during times of respiratory infections, long-term use of invasive ventilation or use of ventilation via a tracheostomy is rare in pediatric LAMA2-RD patients.

nodes.description: An anti-apoptotic small molecule that inhibits the GAPDH-Siah1-mediated death pathway. It is the only therapeutic small molecule to have reached a clinical trial in this disease. In dyW and dy2J mice it inhibits muscle apoptosis, reduces weight loss and skeletal deformity, increases locomotor activity and delays mortality. The human study (CALLISTO, NCT01805024) was a phase 1 open-label pharmacokinetic and safety study over twelve weeks in 20 patients with LAMA2- or COL6-related dystrophy; it met its primary endpoint, but it was neither designed nor powered to show clinical benefit, and none was observed. This is an unapproved investigational agent and is recorded here as the state of the therapeutic pipeline, not as available care.

evidence.snippet: Here we demonstrate that the proapoptotic glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH)-Siah1-CBP/p300-p53 pathway is activated in a mouse model for MDC1A.

nodes.description: Motor nerve conduction velocity is slowed in almost every completely merosin-deficient patient and normal in merosin-positive congenital muscular dystrophy, which is a clean genotype-linked separation. Nerve histology shows short internodes, enlarged nodes, excessive variability of myelin thickness, tomacula and uncompacted myelin without segmental demyelination or onion bulbs, which is the picture of myelin that was built wrongly rather than myelin that was built and then lost. Clinically the neuropathy is mild and adds little to the weakness in humans, in contrast to the mouse, where it is a substantial contributor.

evidence.reference_title: Demyelinating peripheral neuropathy in merosin-deficient congenital muscular dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: All but two of the 10 merosin-deficient cases had reduced motor nerve conduction, whereas all the merosin-positive cases had normal results.

evidence.reference_title: Dysmyelinating sensory-motor neuropathy in merosin-deficient congenital muscular dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Nerve biopsy showed reduction of large myelinated fibers, short internodes, enlarged nodes, excessive variability of myelin thickness, tomacula, and uncompacted myelin, but no evidence of segmental demyelination, naked axons, or onion bulbs.

evidence.reference_title: Dysmyelinating sensory-motor neuropathy in merosin-deficient congenital muscular dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Thus, in congenital muscular dystrophy, merosin expression may be dissociated in different tissues, and the neuropathy is sensory-motor and due to abnormal myelinogenesis.

evidence.reference_title: LAMA2-Related Dystrophies: Clinical Phenotypes, Disease Biomarkers, and Clinical Trial Readiness.
evidence.snippet: Mild, sensorimotor demyelinating neuropathy is commonly observed, but its contribution to muscle weakness is considered to be minimal in the human, while it plays a substantial role in mouse models of lama2 deficiency

nodes.description: Stretching, splinting, orthoses and positioning to slow contracture and preserve what function exists. Given that contracture is driven by early fibrogenesis and accumulates linearly, this is a rate-limiting intervention rather than a preventive one.

evidence.reference_title: LAMA2 Muscular Dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: It is recommended that multidisciplinary care be provided by specialists in neurology, gastroenterology, nutrition, orthopedics, occupational and physical therapy, speech and language therapy, education, psychiatry, pulmonary medicine, cardiology, ophthalmology, and social work.

nodes.description: In a minority of patients the pial basement membrane is not merely thinner but focally breached. Autopsy of an MDC1A brain showed focal disruptions of the glia limitans with abnormal cortical lamination and arrested cerebellar granule cell migration, the classic substrate of a cobblestone malformation, here arising from loss of a structural laminin rather than from defective dystroglycan glycosylation. The module conformance is exact in mechanism: this entry substitutes an absent laminin ligand where the dystroglycanopathies substitute an unglycosylated receptor, and both converge on the same boundary failure.

evidence.reference_title: Cobblestone Malformation in LAMA2 Congenital Muscular Dystrophy (MDC1A).
evidence.snippet: Brain histopathology included focal disruptions of the glia limitans associated with abnormal cerebral cortical lamination or arrested cerebellar granule cell migration.

nodes.description: Polymicrogyria, characteristically occipital, overlapping with the cobblestone malformation and arising from the same pial boundary failure. Where it is extensive it is associated with focal seizures and psychomotor regression.

evidence.snippet: When 6.9 years old, she developed focal occipital seizures and absence-like status when awake, with probable relation to an extensive bilateral occipital micropolygyria.

nodes.description: The organism-level convergence of the muscle arm. Weakness is present from birth and the functional trajectory is dominated less by further loss of strength than by the contractures and spinal deformity that accumulate on top of it: elbow flexor contracture increases linearly with age, and motor regression in the congenital form clusters with the rapid contracture phase between six and nine years. Restrictive respiratory failure follows the same fibrotic-stiffening logic applied to the chest wall and declines at about 2.9% of predicted forced vital capacity per year.

nodes.description: Focal seizures, sometimes secondarily generalised, in roughly 10 to 20% of congenital-form patients and reported more often in the limb-girdle subtype, which is one of the few clinical features that is not simply milder at the milder end of the spectrum. They are usually controlled with first-line antiepileptic drugs when there is no underlying cortical anomaly.

nodes.description: Cobblestone (type II) cortical malformation, typically parieto-occipital and often asymmetric. It was found in six of twelve re-reviewed brain MRIs in one registry cohort, and autopsy shows it can be present even when the clinical MRI was read as structurally normal, so the reported frequency is probably an underestimate of the pathological one.

nodes.description: A partial-deficiency model, carrying a splice mutation that yields a truncated but partly functional protein, with a milder and longer course. It is the natural model for the limb-girdle subtype and the one in which reversibility has been shown: CRISPR-dCas9 upregulation of the paralogous Lama1 improved and partly reversed established fibrosis and hindlimb paralysis when started in symptomatic animals, against the prior expectation that fibrotic change is irreversible.

evidence.reference_title: A mutation-independent approach for muscular dystrophy via upregulation of a modifier gene.
evidence.snippet: We modulate expression of Lama1 in the dy2j/dy2j mouse model of MDC1A using an adeno-associated virus (AAV9) carrying a catalytically inactive Cas9 (dCas9), VP64 transactivators and single-guide RNAs that target the Lama1 promoter.

nodes.description: The complete-null mouse and the most severe of the family, dying by about three weeks. Its value is temporal resolution rather than fidelity of course: it is the model in which the sequence of early events has been mapped, showing apoptosis at postnatal day 1, full dystrophic architecture with inflammation and matrix deposition by day 4, peak deterioration at day 7, and severe involvement of the masticatory muscles that plausibly underlies the malnutrition and death.

evidence.reference_title: Early skeletal muscle pathology and disease progress in the dy(3K)/dy(3K) mouse model of congenital muscular dystrophy with laminin α2 chain-deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Here, we unveil the first pathogenic events and characterise the disease development in a mouse model for LAMA2-CMD (dy3K/dy3K), by analysing muscles at perinatal, neonatal and postnatal stages.

nodes.description: The workhorse preclinical model, expressing a small amount of truncated protein and surviving long enough for intervention studies. Most of the therapeutic hypotheses in this disease were tested here first: Bax deletion and Bcl-2 overexpression, omigapil, integrin alpha-7 overexpression, and the mini-agrin linker. That four mechanistically unrelated interventions each extend survival in the same animal is the strongest single argument that the downstream cascade is attackable.

nodes.description: An optically accessible model whose contribution is direct observation rather than therapeutics. Live tracking of individual fibres showed that detachment is not immediately lethal, since detached fibres retain sarcolemmal integrity and attempt reattachment, extension and fusion before dying, which reframed the disease as having a window in which a detached fibre can be re-functionalised.
